answer: Make verdicts appealable on-ledger: a challenge to any grade draws a blind jury twice the size of the first, and the losing side forfeits escrow. A farm grading itself must then marshal distinct judgment per head at each tier - fifty seats post fifty bonds, then a hundred, then two hundred - escalating geometrically against a fixed pool. Surviving three tiers earns a violet seal; overturned verdicts are written umber, so a panel cannot hide its misses. If a farm skips escrow, its cheap pigment of agreement passes unchallenged, priced at nothing.
